notes: Date: 1 January 1291. Sweden: Magnus Ladulås died on 18 December 1290; his son Birger (b. 1280) reigns under the regency of the marshal Torgils Knutsson. Visby submitted to the crown after the Gotland war of 1288.
Denmark holds northern Estonia (Reval, Wesenberg, Narva) from 1219 to 1346, and Scania (lost to Sweden only in 1332).
Kraków: Przemysł II of Greater Poland has held it since 1290; during 1291 he leaves it to Wenceslaus II of Bohemia. On 1 January it is modelled as Przemysł's.

Silesia (death of Henry IV Probus, 23 June 1290): Henry V the Fat (Legnica-Wrocław), Henry III (Głogów), Bolko I the Strict (Jawor-Świdnica), Bolko I (Opole), Przemysław (Racibórz), Mieszko I (Cieszyn and Oświęcim), Casimir (Bytom); the bishop holds Nysa-Otmuchów. Opava belongs to the Bohemian crown.

North-East Rus': the Grand Prince of Vladimir is Dmitry Alexandrovich of Pereslavl (1283-93), against his brother Andrey of Gorodets. Moscow (Daniel), Tver (Mikhail), Rostov-Uglich, Yaroslavl (Fyodor the Black, also Smolensk), Belozersk, Galich, Ryazan and Murom are appanage principalities tributary to the Horde. Suzdal and Nizhny Novgorod belong to Andrey of Gorodets.
The Golden Horde: Khan Talabuga is overthrown by Nogai and Tokhta during 1291. Nogai rules his own ulus between the Dnieper and the Danube from Isaccea; Bulgaria and Vidin pay him tribute.
Moldavia and Wallachia did not exist yet as states; their lands are under the Tatar ulus of Nogai and local Vlach and Cuman lords (not modelled).
Polotsk and Vitebsk: ruled by princes in the Lithuanian orbit; the details before 1307 are poorly documented (gap).

states.dynasty_note: House of Estridsen. Eric VI, king since 1286 (murder of Eric V at Finderup), rules with the support of his mother Agnes of Brandenburg; northern Estonia is a Danish duchy.

Prince of Volhynia since 1289 (death of Volodymyr Vasylkovych); Lutsk is attached here only through the spread.
Under Tatar baskaks; its princes are not reliably known.

Khan Talabuga (1287-91) rules the right (western) wing; the left wing east of the Ural, the ulus of Orda, is held by Köchü (Konichi) under him. Talabuga is overthrown by Nogai and his protégé Tokhta during 1291.

The beklerbek Nogai, great-grandson of Jochi, rules the western steppe from the Dnieper to the Danube and makes and unmakes khans; Bulgaria and Vidin pay him tribute. His faith: he is said to have accepted Islam, his ulus is largely shamanist.
Genoese colony under Tatar suzerainty since c.1266.
Eastern Georgia under Ilkhanid overlordship; Vakhtang II installed by the Ilkhan after the execution of Demetrius II (1289).
